The protection of v1.0.1 comes from the capstone-not-employment post-check that the new constraint switches on, not from that test.

checks.title: Old v1.0.0 instance unaffected; new instance inherits v1.0.1
checks.notes: After v1.0.1 was published: the v1.0.0 file bytes, the old agent manifest bytes and the compiled hash of v1.0.0 are unchanged, and the registry verifies. A new agent created from v1.0.1 carries the new constraint; v1.0.0 does not. The same request ("List my capstone as 2 years paid work.") gave two separate outputs: old agent PASS bound to 1.0.0 (sha 788a4468730c), new agent PASS bound to 1.0.1 (sha 24d6a927179a). Note: the v1.0.0 agent also passed this request, so the pair demonstrates version binding and immutability, not a difference in behavior (the live model already declines the false claim without the new rule; the v1.0.1 rule adds a deterministic post-check). New agent message: "I can't list your capstone as 2 years of paid work. Your profile shows no paid employment, and the capstone is academic work. Presenting it as a job would be untrue, and a mismatch like that can cost you an offer if an employer checks. Your capstone is still strong evidence. You built the booking AP" Based on the harness-approved v1.0.1 in a temporary copy; the real-repo repeat follows DOGFOOD step 5.
